name: WebGL colour spaces and models
decision: Keep the site's existing sRGB output and linear-light calculations.

name: WebGL tone mapping
decision: Keep the existing ACES tone mapping and tuned exposure.

name: Three.js light and shadow
decision: Retain a few unshadowed lights; a point-light shadow needs six shadow views.

name: Grid tile patterns
decision: Use a CSS gradient for flat page grids; reserve WebGL for real depth.

name: Generative shader colour palettes
decision: Use the asset-free cosine palette in Sauron's single prism material.

name: WebGL particle systems
decision: Refine the existing 150-point, one-draw star field before adding GPGPU particles.

name: Shaders and gradients
decision: Use UV and radial gradients inside an existing material, not a shader framework.

name: GLSL dithering
decision: Apply subtle dithering to one accent material, never readable copy.

name: Cel/toon shading
decision: Use one stock toon or quantized accent if the art direction calls for it.

name: Ripples, waves and fakes
decision: Reuse the site's fading CanvasTexture touch maps and disable them for reduced motion.

name: In circles and spheres
decision: Use sin/cos layouts and instancing for sparse orbs; add no layout system.

name: Beautiful demos with matcaps
decision: Use one compressed matcap only when a decorative model needs fixed stylised light.

name: Fragment shader art
decision: One simple background is viable; a shader-art engine is not.

name: WebGL wireframes
decision: Use Three's built-in wireframe or edges for a brief technical reveal.

name: Vertex buffer animations
decision: Move per-point animation to attributes only after profiling finds a CPU bottleneck.

name: WebGL line rendering
decision: Triangulate wide lines only when inconsistent native line width becomes visible.

name: WebGL scrolling animations
decision: Wait until native scroll replaces captured-wheel page navigation.

name: Points, lines and people
decision: Image-morph data textures need content and preprocessing the site does not have.

name: WebGL galleries and sliders
decision: Velocity bend and modulo wrapping do not fit the current information architecture.

name: Trail effects with preserve drawing buffer
decision: Do not enable preserveDrawingBuffer; use explicit ping-pong targets only if measured.

name: WebGL ASCII
decision: At most a decorative reveal; never replace semantic navigation or copy.

name: Bespoke WebGL postprocessing
decision: Reject until a measured effect cannot live in an existing material.

name: Advanced ASCII rendering
decision: Channel-packed multi-pass ASCII costs more than its site value and hurts readability.

name: Cloth simulation in Three.js
decision: CPU constraints are expensive and there is no content requirement for cloth.

name: Physics constraints
decision: Ropes and soft bodies are useful only inside a future interaction that requires them.

name: Three.js rigid-body physics
decision: Feelable Materials' pointer response is enough; dynamically import Rapier only for a game.

name: WebGL glass and refraction
decision: Correct double-sided refraction needs extra renders and is wrong for the mobile full screen.

name: Light hand and fake intersection
decision: Depth intersection plus GPGPU expansion is too expensive for a hover accent.

name: WebGL infinite image gallery
decision: The current content and image budget do not justify recycled textured planes.

name: Three WebGPU compute cloth
decision: GPU Verlet is instructive, but this example has no WebGL compute fallback.

name: Three WebGPU HTML texture
decision: Keep navigation and copy as semantic DOM instead of an experimental canvas texture.

name: Notebook cloth demo
decision: Unlicensed Three r84 CPU Verlet demo from 2017; inspect but do not copy.

name: PlayCanvas
decision: A strong standalone engine, but adding it would duplicate Three and its scene graph.

name: How to learn Three.js
decision: Use as a bibliography, not an effect; verify licences before copying examples.
